findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so a denial for one identity type can deny another
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name, and parent folder, but not from the identity type. The UserUID is derived by stripping the type prefix from the subject (e.g. "anonymous:0" and "render:0" both yield UserUID "0", and a service account whose UID collides with a user UID is also possible). Because Check consults permDenialCache before anything else and returns Allowed=false immediately on a hit, a denial cached for an anonymous user on "dashboards:read" for some dashboard name will, for the next 30 seconds (shortCacheTTL), also deny the render service for the same action/name even though getRendererPermissions unconditionally grants render read access to dashboards/folders/datasources. The same applies to any cross-type UID collision. The identity type should be included in the denial cache key.

findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits the DB fallback, so newly granted permissions are ignored for up to 30s
findings.body: When a check is denied after a fresh DB lookup, the denial is stored in permDenialCache, and subsequent identical checks return Allowed=false at the top of Check without ever re-querying the permission store — even though the whole point of this PR is to re-query the DB when the cached permissions don't contain the resource. If a user's permission is granted shortly after a denial was cached (e.g. a check raced ahead of the grant write for a just-created dashboard/folder, which is the exact scenario this PR is trying to fix), the user stays denied until the 30-second denial TTL expires, whereas the non-denial path would have picked up the new grant immediately via the DB fallback. Consider skipping the denial-cache fast path when a fresh DB lookup could succeed (or at least documenting/shortening the TTL), since this partially reintroduces the stale-denial problem for creators.

findings.title: Misleading comment in denial-cache test
findings.body: The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the value actually seeded into permCache is map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}, which does not allow access. The test still passes because checkPermission only looks up key presence with a true value, but the comment misdescribes the setup and could confuse future maintainers into thinking cached allows are bypassed when they aren't exercised at all.
